Sara —

Really appreciate Greenline offering to do this. We love customer spotlights. That said, I want to flag one important item before we commit to a publish date or metrics in the copy. We had an incident in late October that affected Greenline’s production environment for about two hours (ticket INF-9876). It was remediated but the customer received a credit and our CS team has been working closely on post-incident follow-up.

Given that context, I need to run a quick sensitivity check internally (sales + CS + legal) before we give a green light to publish any specific numbers or claims. Would you be comfortable if we pause committing to Nov 20 and instead target a confirmation by Nov 15? Alternatively, if Greenline is okay, we could publish a short, sanitized quote that avoids specific uptime/credit/incident language (e.g., a high-level line on developer velocity or reduced latency without the exact percent).

I’m looping in Ava (AM), Rishi (Head of Sales), and Neha (Customer Success leadership) to weigh in.

Thanks for understanding — want to make sure we don’t create any awkward timing for Greenline or Redwood.

— Jonas

Thanks for the tag, Jonas. Quick context from CS — Greenline experienced an availability incident on Oct 20 (INF-9876) that impacted a subset of inference requests for ~2 hours due to a rollout automation bug. We rolled a hotfix, applied credits to their account, and followed up with a post-mortem and mitigation plan. The renewal conversation is ongoing; Greenline has not yet signed the Q1 reserved capacity amendment.

My recommendation is we PAUSE publication of the full case study and any explicit metrics until we have confirmation from the customer that they’re comfortable with public messaging, and until legal has reviewed for sensitivity around the incident. If marketing needs something sooner, offer a 1–2 sentence, non-metric quote from the Greenline marketing team (subject to their sign-off).

If approved, CS will provide a sanitized timeline/statement and the ticket link to Legal. Evelyn can help coordinate the credit/finance details if marketing needs to understand the commercial remediation.
